topic_summary: From 1 July 2026, Division 296 tax applies under the Treasury Laws Amendment (Building a Stronger and Fairer Super System) Act 2026. Individuals with a total super balance (TSB) above the Large Super Balance Threshold (LSBT) of $3,000,000 for 2026-27 face an additional 15% tax on the proportion of earnings above that threshold. Individuals with a TSB above the Very Large Super Balance Threshold (VLSBT) of $10,000,000 for 2026-27 face an additional 10% tax on the proportion of earnings above that threshold. Thresholds are indexed to CPI. Separately, no competitor content explains the tax mechanics, preservation rules, or estate-planning rationale for exiting super into a trust structure — a significant gap for high-net-worth individuals affected by these changes.

terminals.heading: How does Division 296 tax work?
terminals.result_copy: Division 296 tax is an additional tax effective from 1 July 2026. It imposes an additional 15% tax on the proportion of earnings relating to the part of a TSB that exceeds the LSBT of $3,000,000 for 2026-27, and an additional 10% tax on the proportion of earnings relating to the part of a TSB that exceeds the VLSBT of $10,000,000 for 2026-27. Both thresholds are indexed to CPI. The law also changes the definition of total super balance and introduces a new concept called total super balance value. Whether and how these rules apply depends on your individual TSB and earnings — consult the ATO or a qualified adviser for your specific circumstances.

terminals.heading: Will the $3,000,000 and $10,000,000 thresholds change over time?
terminals.result_copy: The Large Super Balance Threshold (LSBT) of $3,000,000 and the Very Large Super Balance Threshold (VLSBT) of $10,000,000 for 2026-27 are both indexed to CPI. Future threshold values cannot be stated here as they depend on CPI movements not yet verified. Monitor ATO announcements or consult a financial adviser for updated thresholds in future years.
